value: det = -(xz - y^2)(p^2 x + 2py + z); it vanishes identically when xz = y^2, i.e. x, y, z in G.P.
note: Sympy factored the 3x3 determinant into exactly two factors. Only the G.P. condition makes it zero for every p. Discriminating checks with the other options all give non-zero: A.P. (1,2,3) at p=1 gives 8 and at p=5 gives 48; H.P. (1,3/2,3) gives -21/4 at p=1 and -39/4 at p=2; the xy,yz,zx-in-A.P. case (1,2,2/3) gives 170/9 at p=1 and 980/9 at p=4. G.P. (1,2,4) and (2,6,18) give 0 at every p tested. The second factor gives the alternative root p = -r (common ratio), a condition on p rather than on x,y,z, so it does not select another option. Stem grammar is loose ('= 0 is' for '= 0 if') but not ambiguous.

|A| = alpha^2 - 4, so |A^3| = (alpha^2-4)^3 = 27 gives alpha^2 - 4 = 3 (the only real cube root), alpha^2 = 7. Substituting each option back: alpha=2 gives |A^3| = 0, sqrt(5) gives 1, 1 gives -27, sqrt(7) gives 27. Only D reproduces 27.

Rows 2 and 3 do not depend on r, so the sum acts only on row 1. Sum over r=0..m gives (m^2-1, 2^m, m+1), which is exactly row 2, so the summed determinant has two identical rows and is 0. Verified by direct summation of the full 3x3 determinant (sin terms included) for m = 1..6: all 0 exactly. Option D 'None of these' is a distractor; 0 is present as B.
Vertices solved exactly: L1&L2 = (6,2), L1&L3 = (-2,3), L2&L3 = (4,7). Shoelace gives area 19 exactly. Lines are not concurrent and the three vertices are distinct.

Symbolic 2x2: A*adj(A) = (ad-bc) I. With |A| = 2 that is 2I regardless of the entries; confirmed on four different matrices of determinant 2, including a non-diagonal and an antidiagonal one, all giving [[2,0],[0,2]].

Exhaustive enumeration of all C(9,3) = 84 draws from 2 white + 3 blue + 4 black: 55 have colour pattern exactly (2,1). Breakdown 1*7 + 3*6 + 6*5 = 7 + 18 + 30 = 55. Matches B exactly; A reduces to 15/28 and C to 5/12, neither equal to 55/84.
9 balls total (3+4+2). Enumerated all C(9,2) = 36 pairs; 3 are white-white, so probability = 3/36 = 1/12. No two options are equal.

Exhaustive weighted enumeration over 4^3 * 2^2 = 256 equally likely tick patterns: P(all 5) = 1/256, P(exactly 4) = 11/256 (3 ways a 4-option question is wrong at 3/256 each, plus 2 ways a true/false is wrong at 1/256 each), total 12/256 = 3/64. Exact rational arithmetic, no floating point.

Four equally likely (a,b) pairs. Discriminants b^2-4a: (1,1) -> -3, (1,2) -> 0, (2,1) -> -7, (2,2) -> -4. Only (a,b) = (1,2) gives real (repeated) roots, so 1/4. Note the single favourable case is the boundary disc = 0; 'real roots' includes equal real roots, which is the standard reading.

value: None of the three formulas is a general identity for P(A and B)
note: Tested each candidate on 300 random finite probability spaces with random events: option A failed 291/300, option B 292/300, option C 296/300. Simple counterexample with A = B and P(A) = 1/2: P(A and B) = 1/2 while A gives 1/2 - 1/2 = 0, B gives 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, C gives 1. The correct identity would be P(A)+P(B)-P(A or B), which is not offered, so D is right.
Enumerated all 720 permutations of 4 distinct boys and 2 distinct girls in a row; 240 have the girls in adjacent seats, giving 240/720 = 1/3. Matches the closed form 2!*5!/6! = 1/3.

value: P(C|D) = P(C)/P(D) >= P(C), since C is a subset of D and 0 < P(D) <= 1
note: Over 400 random spaces with C a subset of D: option D held 400/400, option A (strict <) held 0/400, option C (equality) held only 15/400 and option B only 38/400 - both only in the degenerate cases where P(D) = 1 or the ratio coincides. C is the trap: equality holds only when P(D) = 1, so the general statement is the inequality in D.
Sum = 49 over 7 values, so mean = 7 exactly. Absolute deviations 4,3,3,3,0,3,2 sum to 18, mean deviation = 18/7 = 2.5714. Option B states 2.57, the rounded value; no other option is within 0.4.

Computed directly from the 20 values with exact rationals: mean 21/2, variance 133/4, agreeing with (n^2-1)/12 = 399/12 = 133/4. Option B is 279/12 = 23.25 (not the same as 399/12, which would have been a duplicate of A), C is 66.5, D is 99.75. Only A matches.

From sec^2 - tan^2 = 1, (sec - tan)(sec + tan) = 1 so sec - tan = 1/p; adding to sec + tan = p gives 2 sec = p + 1/p. Sympy confirms the expression minus sec(theta) simplifies to 0 identically. Numerically at theta = 0.3, 0.7, 1.0, 1.4, 1.5 (30 dps) option C reproduces sec(theta) to all digits while A, B, D do not - checked at several theta because A drifts toward 1 for large p and could look plausible at a single point.
